answer: Sybil resistance can work through proof-of-work stamps tied to physical resource costs: each new agent identity must solve a challenge that consumes measurable compute, and the resulting proof is anchored to a unique hardware fingerprint. An attacker forging a thousand identities on one machine hits a cost ridge, because each stamp demands fresh power and time. Peers also cross-check a pigment of behavioral history and copper-backed stake deposits, so fake identities must pay real collateral, making mass forgery economically unprofitable.
